## Problem

When a new project is created (or an existing one initialized) with an AGENTS.md, the current installer/template behavior emits the full duplicated instruction set as a local file. This is how the four sibling projects ended up with large local AGENTS.md files that duplicate the global one (see SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G, SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N).

## User story

As a developer creating a new project, I want the AGENTS.md installer to emit only the canonical global-reference structure so new projects never start by duplicating the global rules.

# Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via helper report skill

## Problem statement

Every skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, ship, etc.) currently ends its session with an ad-hoc, inconsistently formatted summary. Producers must re-scan raw output to extract status, acceptance-criteria verdicts, and next actions. This work standardizes the end-of-session report into a single, quickly scannable format produced by a shared helper skill that other skills call.

## Users

- **Producers/operators** who review the end of every skill session and need to quickly scan: what was done, are acceptance criteria met, what state is the work item in, what actions (if any) are required of them.
- **Agents/skills** that need a canonical, reusable report template with deterministic metadata (avoiding each skill inventing its own format).

### User stories

- As a producer, I want every skill session to end with the same report structure, so I can scan results quickly without re-reading raw session output.
- As a skill author, I want a helper skill that provides the canonical report template and metadata (type, priority, status, stage, risk, effort, children, audit), so my skill produces compliant reports with minimal effort.
- As a producer, I want to see the acceptance criteria with per-criterion met/unmet verdicts, so I can tell at a glance whether the work item is ready.
- As a producer, I want an explicit "Producer Actions" section, so I know exactly what (if anything) I need to do next.
- As a producer, I want a freeform Notes section, so the agent can surface context, caveats, or assumptions that don't fit the structured sections.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new helper skill (e.g., `skill/report/` or `skill/session-report/`) exists with a SKILL.md defining the canonical end-of-session report format exactly as specified: header `# Completed <skill_name>`, work-item title + id, headline summary, `## Acceptance Criteria` table, `## Meta-Data`, `## Producer Actions`, `## Notes`, `## Conclusion`.
- [ ] The report template matches the requested layout: AC rows are `|<ac#>|<Description>|<Metric>|<met|unmet>|`; Meta-Data lists Type, Priority, Status, Stage, Risk, Effort, Children, Audit each as `<icon> <text>`; Producer Actions defaults to `None needed`; Notes is freeform; Conclusion states `<This completes the <skill_name> process for <id> (<title>). Ready for <next_action>.`
- [ ] The report includes the `## Notes` section between `## Producer Actions` and `## Conclusion` for freeform agent commentary.
- [ ] Meta-Data values (Type, Priority, Status, Stage, Risk, Effort, Children, Audit) are populated deterministically from the work item (via `wl show <id> --json`), so the report reflects the current worklog state rather than the agent's memory.
- [ ] **Icon mappings match the canonical ContextHub set** (`../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` / `src/icons.ts`, the set used by the `wl` CLI itself): priority 🚨/⭐/📋/🐢, status 🔓/🔄/✔️/⛔/🗑️/💬, stage 💡/📥/📋/🛠️/🔍/🏁, risk 🌱/⚠️/🔥/🚨, effort 🐜/🐇/🐕/🐘/🐋, audit ✅/❌/❔, with bracketed text fallbacks (`[CRIT]`, `[OPEN]`, `[IDEA]`, `[LOW]`, `[XS]`, `[YES]`, etc.) when icons are unavailable. The helper documents the full mapping table and its ContextHub source so the sets cannot drift. (ContextHub already provides this shared helper — `src/icons.ts` + `docs/icons-design.md` — so no new ContextHub work item is required; see Related work.)
- [ ] The helper skill documents a clear invocation contract (how another skill calls it at the end of its session — e.g., a short embeddable instruction block) that skills embed as their final step.
- [ ] **All existing skills that work on work-items are wired to invoke the helper** at the end of their session, each with its SKILL.md updated to reference the helper: intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, and author-command (any skill whose flow creates/updates work items). Verification: grep across `skill/*/SKILL.md` shows every work-item skill ends with the standardized report instruction.
- [ ] A test validates the report renderer: given a work item + AC verdicts, it produces the expected report structure (sections present, AC table rows, metadata icons/values, defaults for empty fields).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including the new skill's SKILL.md, README, and any references in migrated skills.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The helper skill is invoked by other skills; it does not replace a skill's own workflow or status lifecycle management.
- The report is produced at the end of a skill session; it should not require new work-item state changes beyond what the calling skill already performs.
- Report must remain scannable: prose sections (headline, Notes) are concise; structured sections carry the details.
- Keep it simple: a single template + metadata renderer (script or documented wl command) is sufficient; no orchestration framework.
- Icon mappings are sourced from ContextHub's canonical set — do not invent new icons in individual skills.

## Existing state

- Skills currently end sessions with ad-hoc summaries: e.g., implement closes with `<work-item-id>: <concise-summary> / Work committed to dev`; intake ends with an Objective/AC/Effort-Risk summary; audit has its own persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, `## Summary`, `## Acceptance Criteria Status`).
- No shared report template or helper skill exists (`grep` for `## Producer Actions` / `## Meta-Data` / `## Conclusion` across `skill/*/SKILL.md` returns nothing).
- Worklog exposes all needed metadata via `wl show <id> --json` (issueType, priority, status, stage, risk, effort, childCount, auditResult/audit status).
- Effort/risk use t-shirt sizes (XS–XL) from `skill/effort-and-risk/references/t-shirt_sizes.json`; risk levels are low/medium/high.
- **ContextHub already provides the canonical icon set**: `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` (spec) and `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` (TypeScript implementation), consumed by the `wl` CLI (`dist/icons.js`). Mappings cover priority, status, stage, risk, effort, audit, epic, and producer-review flags, each with emoji + bracketed text fallback + accessible label.
- Skills live in `skill/<name>/SKILL.md` with optional `scripts/` and `tests/`; global install symlinks `~/.pi/agent/skills` → this repo's `skill/` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Desired change

1. Create `skill/report/SKILL.md` (or `skill/session-report/`) defining:
   - The canonical report template (exact section order and layout as specified, including `## Notes` before `## Conclusion`).
   - Icon mappings per Meta-Data field sourced from ContextHub's canonical set (`../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` / `src/icons.ts`), with bracketed text fallbacks.
   - Instructions for populating each section (AC verdicts from the calling skill's own evaluation; Meta-Data from `wl show --json`).
   - A short "how to invoke" contract that other skills embed (e.g., a call-out block to add to a skill's final step).
2. Provide `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (or a documented `wl show` + template recipe) that renders the Meta-Data block deterministically from `wl show <id> --json` — helpers to extract/format metadata, icons (reusing ContextHub mappings), and defaults.
3. Wire the helper into **all** work-item skills: update each `skill/*/SKILL.md` (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command) so the final step invokes the standardized report.
4. Add tests (e.g., `skill/report/tests/`) validating the template and metadata rendering.
5. Add an example rendered report in the SKILL.md so agents can copy the pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — new helper skill defining the canonical report format, ContextHub-sourced icon mappings, and invocation contract.
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — metadata renderer reading `wl show --json`, reusing ContextHub icon mappings.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — tests for template structure, metadata icons, defaults.
- `skill/<name>/SKILL.md` for every work-item skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command) — final step invokes the helper report.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — its existing persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, AC status table) is the closest precedent; reconcile its end-of-session summary with the new template.

## Related work

- `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` + `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` — **canonical icon set** (priority, status, stage, risk, effort, audit, epic, producer-review) with emoji + text fallbacks + accessible labels; consumed by the `wl` CLI. The report skill reuses these mappings. (This is the shared helper the requirement asks for — no new ContextHub work item needed.)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — existing persisted report format (`Ready to close:` header, `## Summary`, `## Acceptance Criteria Status` table, `## Variance Decisions`, `## Children Status`); the closest existing structured-report precedent to reconcile/align with.
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — defines risk (low/medium/high) and effort t-shirt (XS–XL) values used in the Meta-Data section.
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — example helper skill with scripts + tests + a "compact report" pattern.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — skills' shared status/stage transitions; the report's Status/Stage metadata reflects these.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** wiring the helper into every work-item skill is broad; the requirement is explicit, so all work-item skills are in scope for this item. Skills that do not touch work items (e.g., speak) are excluded.
- **Icon consistency:** icon mappings must come from the ContextHub canonical set (single source of truth) to avoid per-skill divergence; the helper documents the mapping table + source. Unknown values fall back to a neutral marker; icons are decorative — the textual value always accompanies them, so reports remain readable in non-emoji terminals/views.
- **Metadata drift:** report reflects the worklog at render time; if the calling skill changes state after rendering, the report may be stale. Mitigation: render the report as the final step of the session.
- **Audit reconciliation:** audit's existing persisted format differs (it is machine-verified). Its end-of-session summary is reconciled with the template; its persisted machine-verified report format is preserved.
- **Assumption:** Meta-Data is rendered deterministically from worklog where possible; the agent supplies only prose (headline, Notes, Producer Actions, Conclusion next-action).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which skill should be the first adopter / what is the migration scope?" — Answer (operator, 2026-08-07): "Add an AC that wires the helper into all existing skills that work on work-items." The migration scope is therefore ALL work-item skills, not just 1–2 adopters. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What icon mappings should be used?" — Answer (operator, 2026-08-07): "Icon mappings should be the same as those used in ../ContextHub. If that project does not have a shared helper you can use then create a work item in that project to do so and make this work item dependent upon it." Research: ContextHub provides the canonical icon set in `../ContextHub/docs/icons-design.md` and `../ContextHub/src/icons.ts` (consumed by the `wl` CLI), covering all Meta-Data fields. No new ContextHub work item is required — the helper references that set. Source: interactive reply + repo inspection.
- Q: "Should the report be persisted (e.g., work-item comment) or stdout only?" — Answer: pending (proposed default: stdout only for v1; persistence as follow-up). Source: interactive reply (asked 2026-08-07).
- Q: "Should Meta-Data be auto-generated from `wl show --json`?" — Answer: pending (proposed default: yes, via a small renderer script). Source: interactive reply (asked 2026-08-07).

**Summary:** The audit freshness gate (skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`) keys freshness on the whole-repo git HEAD sha. ANY commit to the repo — even one touching files unrelated to the work item — changes HEAD, invalidates the content fingerprint, and forces a full two-phase re-audit. This caused a real false re-audit: NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U was audited "Ready to close: No" (AC5 partial), the content fingerprint was byte-identical on re-audit, yet an operator `/skill:audit` invocation re-ran the full pipeline (twice, dry-run and persisted), and the final persisted verdict flipped to "Ready to close: Yes" purely from model judgment variance on the same unverifiable AC — no new evidence. A freshness gate that actually asserted "the work is in HEAD" would have returned the stored verdict.

**Desired behavior:** freshness must be decided per work item, not per repo. If NO file touched by the work item has changed since the work was committed, the stored audit verdict stands — no re-audit, no model calls. If any touched file changed, the audit is stale and re-runs.

**User stories:**
- As an operator running `/skill:audit <id>` on an item whose work files are unchanged, I want the stored verdict returned in seconds so unrelated repo commits never trigger an expensive re-audit.
- As an operator, I want the gate to be strict about the work item itself: any change to files the item touched (or to its ACs/description/Key Files) must invalidate freshness.

**How to determine "files touched by the work item":**
1. Commits referencing the work item ID: `git log --all --grep=<id>` and/or the commit messages recorded on the work item comments (implement skill already records commit hashes). The union of files in those commits = touched files.
2. The Key Files section of the work item description (already parsed by `_extract_key_files`).
3. Fallback: if touched-file set cannot be determined (no commits recorded, git unavailable), fail open and re-run the pipeline (current behavior).

**Suggested approach (strict-mode fingerprint):** extend `_compute_content_fingerprint` to a payload of {touched-file set (paths + per-path current git blob hashes or latest commit touching each path), description_hash, key_files} instead of the bare repo HEAD sha. On freshness check, recompute per-path state; equality => fresh. Document trade-offs: the gate is no longer fail-open-cheap the same way, and tool-artifact rewrites (e.g. Unity batch runs rewriting ProjectSettings, see Nova AGENTS.md pitfall #4) must be tolerated — e.g. exclude known tool-artifact paths or accept that they invalidate freshness (safe direction: stale => re-run is never wrong, only wasteful).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] (AC1) Freshness gate decides freshness from the work item touched-file set, not the bare repo HEAD sha: a commit touching only unrelated files does NOT invalidate a stored audit with an unchanged fingerprint
- [ ] (AC2) Any change to a file in the touched-file set invalidates freshness and re-runs the pipeline
- [ ] (AC3) Work-item description/AC/Key Files changes still invalidate freshness (existing behavior preserved)
- [ ] (AC4) Touched-file set resolution falls back to fail-open (re-run pipeline) when it cannot be determined (no recorded commits, git unavailable)
- [ ] (AC5) Tool-artifact rewrites (e.g. ProjectSettings churn from Unity batch runs) are handled explicitly — either excluded from the touched-file comparison or documented as always-invalidating with a test
- [ ] (AC6) Unit tests cover: unrelated-commit freshness (AC1), touched-file change invalidation (AC2), description-change invalidation (AC3), and fail-open fallback (AC4)
- [ ] (AC7) Re-audit of NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U at unchanged state returns the stored verdict without re-running the pipeline (regression scenario from this issue)

# Local Skill Extensions for Global Skills

## Problem

Global skills (intake, plan, implement, audit, etc.) provided by this project are static and cannot be extended per-project without modifying the global skill files directly. There is currently no mechanism to customize or extend global skills with project-specific behavior.

## Goal

Enable project-level extension of global skills through convention-based files, allowing each project to augment global skills with local behavior without modifying the core skill files.

## Proposed Approach

## Goal

Reduce wasted re-audit work in the release pipeline: audits that are redundant (item already audited at the same HEAD) or stale (code changed after the audit) currently trigger full re-runs — each costing 15-45 min of model time. Make re-audits the exception, not the norm.

## Background (observed during 2026-08-12 release of SorraAgents)

1. **Redundant audit by a second session**: Map re-audited SA-0MSOK041Z0027964 (already completed + audited by another session at the same HEAD, verdict Ready to close: Yes, ~19:00). ~1 hour of model time spent repeating a passed audit. Root cause: no coordination check (`wl audit-show` / status / comments) before launching a re-audit, and no fast-path that short-circuits when a fresh audit already exists.
2. **Stale audits after post-audit commits**: the 9 children of SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ were audited, then 2 more commits landed on dev (49a32769 test-fix, e7266ccc AC1 scoping) touching the same files — every one of the 9 audits went stale and had to be re-run (~2.5 h of audits). Root cause: audit freshness is keyed on the audited file content, but the fingerprint did not incorporate the commit/HEAD at audit time; SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ (working-tree state in fingerprint, completed) is the first step but does not yet key freshness on commit hash.
3. **Transient/timeout re-runs**: SA-0MSM6VU2K001IMVP and the parent SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ audit-1 both timed out under model contention and were re-run once the slot freed — unavoidable, but a queue/slot-stagger hint would reduce the retry rate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` records the git commit hash (HEAD) at audit time in the persisted audit record; freshness check considers an audit stale if HEAD moved since the audit ran (in addition to content fingerprint).
2. Before starting a full audit, the runner (or the audit skill docs) surfaces an existing fresh audit: `wl audit-show <id>` shows "Ready to close: Yes" with auditedAt >= last commit touching audited files → the runner prints a fast-path notice and exits (or prompts) instead of re-running the model.
3. `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and the audit skill reference docs document the coordination check: always run `wl audit-show <id>` + `wl comment list <id>` first; do not re-audit an item that is completed/in_review with a fresh audit unless the code changed.
4. Measurable: re-audit count in one release cycle drops (target: 0 redundant re-audits — only stale/forced re-audits allowed); verified by a test that audits twice at the same HEAD and asserts the second run short-circuits without invoking the model.

## Out of scope

- Changing audit verdict semantics or the audit gate itself.
- Fixing model-contention timeouts (separate concern, tracked elsewhere).
- The two currently-open critical items blocking release (SA-0MSQ72BVV0011SRU, SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T).

Related: SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ (working-tree fingerprint — first step, completed); discovered during release work on SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ.
